text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone who works with it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so others can quickly see what they do. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because fixing bugs or adding new features becomes less risky. In short, writing clean code helps your whole team work faster.
